/-!
# Erdős Problem 152

#TODO: Formalize the corresponding conjecture for infinite Sidon sets.

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/152](https://www.erdosproblems.com/152)
 - [DM26a] DeepMind prover agent, [formal proof of Erdős problem 152](https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/29c60aa79729701905cf9e92517af23f588971f2/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/152.lean#L485) (2026)
 - [DM26b] DeepMind prover agent, [formal proof of the quadratic variant of Erdős problem 152](https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/ff58c933d53bb807bf85d98a47402703f9f14ed3/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/152.lean#L496) (2026)
 - [ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number
    Theory (1994), 329-347.
-/

open scoped Pointwise Asymptotics
open Filter

namespace Erdos152

/-- Define `f n` to be the minimum of `|{s | s - 1 ∉ A + A, s ∈ A + A, s + 1 ∉ A + A}|` as `A`
ranges over all Sidon sets of size `n`. -/
noncomputable def f (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ⨅ A : {A : Set ℕ | A.ncard = n ∧ IsSidon A},
  {s : ℕ | s - 1 ∉ A.1 + A.1 ∧ s ∈ A.1 + A.1 ∧ s + 1 ∉ A.1 + A.1}.ncard

/--
Must `lim f n = ∞`?

This was proved formally by the DeepMind prover agent [DM26a].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/29c60aa79729701905cf9e92517af23f588971f2/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/152.lean#L485"]
theorem erdos_152 : answer(True) ↔ Tendsto f atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Must `f n ≫ n ^ 2`?

This stronger quadratic variant was also proved formally by the DeepMind prover agent [DM26b].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/ff58c933d53bb807bf85d98a47402703f9f14ed3/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/152.lean#L496"]
theorem erdos_152.variants.square : answer(True) ↔
    (fun n => f n : ℕ → ℝ) ≫ (fun n => n ^ 2 : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos152

reformulations.difference: The source quantifies over every sufficiently large finite Sidon set of positive integers. Lean instead takes the minimum count over sets of each natural-number cardinality and asserts that these minima tend to infinity. Allowing zero and using truncated subtraction can omit an isolated sum at zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let I(A) be the count used in Lean and J(A) the ordinary isolated-sum count, allowing zero to be isolated. For finite A, I(A) ≤ J(A) ≤ I(A)+1. Translation A ↦ {a+1 | a∈A} preserves cardinality, the Sidon property, and J(A), so the positive-integer convention is immaterial. Sidon sets exist at every finite size; the natural-valued infimum is an attained minimum. For n>0, A.ncard=n implies finiteness. Consequently, Tendsto f atTop atTop implies the source's uniform bound, while the source applied with M+1 gives the converse despite the possible lost sum. The complete equivalence, including answer(True), was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review152.main_full_statement_equivalence.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for a uniform quadratic lower bound on isolated sums in sufficiently large finite Sidon sets. Lean expresses this as n² = O(f(n)), using the minimum function and the same natural-number boundary convention.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Because both functions are nonnegative, the repository's ≫ notation is equivalent to ∃ c>0, ∃ N, ∀ n≥N, c*n² ≤ f(n). Taking the minimum is equivalent to requiring the bound uniformly over all sets of that size. Translation handles positive versus nonnegative integers. The inequality J(A) ≤ I(A)+1 shows that a source bound J(A) ≥ c*|A|² implies I(A) ≥ (c/2)*|A|² once c*|A|²≥2; the reverse follows from I(A)≤J(A). Thus the possible one-sum discrepancy changes neither claim. The complete equivalence, including answer(True), was proved as Review152.square_full_statement_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations. Both solved tags, affirmative answers, and cited proof records agree with the source. Scratch proofs establish nonempty minimization families, attainment, f(0)=0, f(1)=0, and both source equivalences; their axiom lists contain only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Computable finite-set examples and bounded searches were also tested. Although f is not pointwise identical to the minimum for positive-integer sets at small sizes, the source does not prescribe a named function f, and both actual claims are provably equivalent. The infinite-set variant is explicitly left as a TODO. No files under /opt/formal-conjectures were edited.
